What happens when an Indian aerospace supplier starts finding opportunities beyond aerospace? ✈️🔌

Meet Rossell Techsys — a Bengaluru-based engineering and manufacturing company working across aerospace, defence and now semiconductor applications.

The interesting part is how quickly its business is expanding.

In August, Rossell Techsys received its first order from a newly onboarded global semiconductor customer to manufacture electrical wire harnesses. The order is for 12 months, and the company said it could lead to additional opportunities as the relationship develops.

That comes after a strong Q1 FY27.

Revenue from operations reached approximately ₹154.5 crore, up about 77% year-on-year, while profit for the period rose more than 116% to around ₹7.1 crore.

The company ended FY26 with roughly ₹485 crore in revenue, while management disclosed long-term strategic agreements of around ₹3,000 crore and confirmed orders of approximately ₹715 crore at year-end.

And there is another development worth watching: Rossell Techsys has scheduled a board meeting for September 18 to consider a proposal for preferential issuance of equity shares.

From aircraft and defence systems to semiconductor manufacturing, the story is becoming much broader.

Could India’s aerospace supply chain gradually evolve into a wider high-precision manufacturing ecosystem? 🇮🇳
